# list ping and the rest of the game do not change. With no one registered, both go straight through.

# Stein FPS: a server with a packet limit disconnected). And options.txt is written there at most every 250 ms.

# Freeze watchdog (engine/Watchdog): counts what arrives from the server (Packet.processPacket inside
# NetworkManager.channelRead0), what goes out, and the game ticks. When the player is in a world and all of this stops, the
# watchdog dumps the threads to the log — it is the only way to see a bottlenecked thread. What goes out passes through two
# writeAndFlush calls: the one in dispatchPacket, when already on the network thread, and the one in the deferred Runnable (ek$4.run), through
# which almost everything goes — the game sends packets from the game thread. The first alone would give 9 packets in half a minute.

# outside it the game keeps toggling sprint as usual.

# Ghost ally (Stein Combat, with the hide key on): RendererLivingEntity.renderModel
# (bjl.a(Lpr;FFFFFF)V) already chooses between drawing normally, not drawing, and drawing at 15% without writing
# depth — the ghost the game makes of someone who is invisible and on your team. The two questions that
# lead to that choice go through the mods, and only inside that method: isInvisible() and
# isInvisibleToPlayer(player). That way the ghost is the game's own, with its code.
pr
pr
# And the layers (armor, held item, cape) do not come out on the ghost: the game draws them outside
# invisibility — which is why an invisible player in armor becomes "walking armor" —, and a 15% silhouette
# with solid armor on top would show nothing of what is behind it.
bjl
# The ghost does not burn on screen (Render.doRenderShadowAndFire, biv.b(Lpk;DDDFF)V): the flames are drawn
# outside the model, like the armor, and a 15% silhouette inside a solid fire is the opposite of what the
# ghost does. It keeps burning for the server and everything else.
pk
# And it does not emit potion particles (EntityLivingBase.updatePotionEffects, pr.bi()V): without the potion color the game
# emits none. The game already emits fewer for someone invisible — one in fifteen —, but "fewer" still marks
# where the person is.
pz
# The ghost does not flash red when taking damage (RendererLivingEntity.doRender, bjl.a(Lpr;DDDFF)V): the
# setDoRenderBrightness paints the whole model before drawing — red from the hit, white from the creeper, dark
# from death — and the game unpaints afterwards. Answering that nothing was painted leaves nothing to unpaint.
bjl
